title: Annual Large Bank Capital Requirements - Federal Reserve Board
summary: The Federal Reserve Board describes its capital framework for large bank holding companies, savings and loan holding companies, and U.S. intermediate holding companies with $100 billion or more in total consolidated assets. The total CET1 capital ratio requirement consists of three components: a minimum 4.5% CET1 requirement, a stress capital buffer (SCB) of at least 2.5% derived from supervisory stress test results, and a G-SIB capital surcharge of at least 1.0% for global systemically important banks. Note: Actual current capital requirements are contained in linked PDF documents.
key_points: Large bank capital requirements apply to institutions with $100 billion or more in total consolidated assets
CET1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum 4.5% floor applicable to all banks
Stress capital buffer (SCB) requirement is at least 2.5% and is derived from supervisory stress test results
G-SIB capital surcharge is at least 1.0% for global systemically important banks
Category IV firms were required to participate in the 2026 supervisory stress test even though they typically are not required in odd years
SCB requirements are based on 2022 stress test results
why_it_matters: This framework establishes the capital buffers that large banks must maintain, directly affecting their ability to absorb losses and potentially influencing lending capacity. The SCB and G-SIB surcharges create differentiated capital requirements based on each bank's risk profile and systemic importance. Market participants monitor these requirements as they affect bank profitability targets, dividend capacities, and risk appetite. Note: Specific current-period capital requirement numbers are available in the linked PDF documents.
market_structure_context: The capital requirements framework is a core element of banking market structure, determining minimum capital buffers that large banks must hold. This affects the competitive landscape by creating tiered requirements based on bank size and systemic importance. Actual capital requirement values for specific banks are documented in the linked PDF files.
